summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of polymyositis, morbid obesity, chronic heart failure, diabetes, and long-term anticoagulation was admitted for a painful right axillary abscess. She reported a one-week history of a growing lump and subjective fevers. Imaging confirmed a 4.8 cm fluid collection, and she underwent ultrasound-guided aspiration, yielding 20 cc of pus. Cultures grew Morganella morganii, resistant to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, with mixed flora on gram stain. Due to persistent fluid on follow-up ultrasound, she underwent incision and drainage. Antibiotics were adjusted from vancomycin to piperacillin-tazobactam and then transitioned to oral doxycycline, ciprofloxacin, and metronidazole. Warfarin was held initially, then restarted with heparin bridging, achieving a therapeutic INR by discharge. Her chronic conditions were managed without complication. She was discharged home with oral antibiotics, pain control, dressing changes, and home health support.
